name: Three-quarter top-down
why: The camera looks down at roughly 45-60 degrees, so a unit reads from a single drawn facing that is mirrored horizontally for the opposite direction. This is the cheapest projection per unit of visual quality, and it is the native habitat of the cel-shaded-outline style.

facings.note: Two drawn facings cover walking toward and away from the camera; east/west is one drawing plus a horizontal flip. Diagonals are approximated by the nearest facing.

render.shadow: blob shadow sprite under the unit
render.notes: Godot: a single Y-sorted CanvasLayer with TileMapLayer beneath. Depth comes from draw order, not from the tile grid.

sim_contract.coordinates: logical grid cells; the renderer maps cell -> pixel, the simulation never sees pixels
